title: Module 7: Importing and Integrating
description: Bringing external data into ServiceNow with Import Sets (staging tables and Transform Maps) and integrating via web services (REST/SOAP, ServiceNow as consumer and provider, the Table API, and the REST API Explorer).

questions.prompt: When data is brought in using an import set, where does it land first?

choices.text: Directly in the destination production table
In a temporary staging table called the import set table
In a read-only audit table that is reviewed and then permanently archived
In an attachment record on the importing user

questions.explanation: Import sets load source data into a temporary staging table (the import set table) rather than straight into the target. The staging step converts the data into GlideRecords and lets you validate it before transforming it into the destination table.

questions.prompt: What is the correct sequence for importing data with an import set?

choices.text: Run Transform, then Load Data, then Create Transform Map
Create Transform Map, then Run Transform, then Load Data
Load Data, then Create Transform Map, then Run Transform
Load Data, then Run Transform, then Create Transform Map

questions.explanation: First load the source data into the import set table, then create (or reuse) a Transform Map that maps the staging fields to the target fields, then run the transform to copy the data into the destination table.

questions.prompt: What is a Transform Map?

choices.text: A scheduled job that periodically reloads data from the source file
A set of field maps defining the relationships between import-set fields and target-table fields
A security rule that controls who may run an import
A staging table that temporarily stores the imported rows

questions.explanation: A Transform Map is a set of field map records that determine how fields in the import set table relate to fields in an existing target table. Once defined it can be reused, and multiple maps can be stacked for more complex transformations.

questions.prompt: The "Auto map matching fields" utility can map fields automatically under which condition?

choices.text: When the source field names match the target field names
When the target table extends the Task table
When the import set contains exactly two columns
When the source file is provided in CSV format with a defined header row

questions.explanation: Auto map matching fields works when the import-set field names are identical to the target-table field names; one click then creates the field maps. Any mismatches can be corrected afterward with the Mapping Assist utility.

questions.prompt: Which capability is unique to the Mapping Assist utility compared with auto-mapping?

choices.text: It runs business rules during the transform
It automatically cleans and corrects invalid data in the staging table before the import runs
It can map a single source field to multiple destination fields
It skips records that already exist in the target

questions.explanation: Mapping Assist provides a visual environment for specifying field maps manually, including mapping one source field to several destination fields. Auto-mapping only pairs fields whose names already match exactly.

questions.prompt: By default (with Enforce mandatory fields left off), how does a transform handle a row whose value for a normally-mandatory target field is empty?

choices.text: It still inserts the record even though the mandatory field is empty
It deletes the corresponding record from the target table
It halts the entire transform and raises an error until a value is supplied for the field
It substitutes a system default value into the field

questions.explanation: Imports can insert records even when normally-mandatory fields are empty. The Enforce mandatory fields option exists precisely to make the transform enforce mandatory-ness (as if the record were submitted from a form) when that stricter behavior is wanted.

questions.prompt: What does enabling "Run business rules" on a Transform Map do?

choices.text: It validates the source file before loading it into the staging table
It restricts the transform to administrators only
It runs business rules, workflows, approvals, auditing, and field normalization as records are inserted or updated into the target table
It forces all field maps to be created automatically

questions.explanation: When selected, the transformation triggers business rules, workflows/flows, approval engines, auditing, and field normalization as it writes to the target table, rather than performing a silent data load.

questions.prompt: What does the import process do when the data being imported is the same as the data already in the instance?

choices.text: It duplicates the record so both copies are kept
It skips the record
It raises a transform error and stops
It moves the existing record to an archive table

questions.explanation: The import process skips records when the incoming data matches what is already in the instance, avoiding redundant inserts or updates.

questions.prompt: As a web service provider, which mechanisms does the Now Platform support? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Direct web services
Web service import set
Scripted web services
Outbound REST message

questions.explanation: As a provider, ServiceNow supports direct web services (access to table structures), web service import sets (input-only, invoking Transform Maps), and scripted web services (custom JavaScript). An outbound REST message is how ServiceNow acts as a consumer, not a provider.

questions.prompt: To consume a third-party web service from ServiceNow, what do you create?

choices.text: A new inbound web service
A new scripted REST resource
A new Outbound REST Message
A new Transform Map

questions.explanation: When ServiceNow is the consumer, you create an Outbound REST Message that defines the provider's endpoint and authentication. Inbound and scripted REST resources are used when ServiceNow is the provider.

questions.prompt: Which statement about REST and SOAP is correct?

choices.text: ServiceNow can act as a SOAP provider but never as a SOAP consumer
SOAP is generally stricter and supports capabilities such as batch processing that REST does not
REST stands for Reliable External Service Transport
REST always requires the exchange of SSL certificates for authentication, whereas SOAP cannot use any security at all

questions.explanation: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) is older and stricter and offers things like batch processing and additional WS-Security; REST (REpresentational State Transfer) is the common modern framework. ServiceNow supports SOAP as both consumer and provider.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method corresponds to reading/retrieving data?

choices.text: POST
PUT
GET
DELETE

questions.explanation: GET retrieves (reads) data from the endpoint. POST creates, PUT/PATCH update, and DELETE removes.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the PUT and PATCH HTTP methods?

choices.text: PUT replaces the entire record/resource, while PATCH applies a partial update
PUT applies a partial update to selected fields, while PATCH replaces the entire record
PUT creates a record, while PATCH deletes one
PUT reads a record, while PATCH writes one

questions.explanation: Both are updates, but PUT is a complete overwrite/replacement of the resource, whereas PATCH modifies only part of it. (In ServiceNow's own database an update is just an update; the distinction is at the HTTP level.)

questions.prompt: Which server-side JavaScript class does the generated outbound REST stub use to send a request?

choices.text: GlideRecord
sn_ws.RESTMessageV2
GlideAjax
XMLDocument2

questions.explanation: Outbound REST requests in script use the RESTMessageV2 class (sn_ws.RESTMessageV2), with methods such as setStringParameterNoEscape(), execute(), getBody(), and getStatusCode(). XMLDocument2 is used to parse an XML response, not to send the request.

questions.prompt: In an HTTP Query Parameter value on a REST method, what does enclosing the value in ${ } accomplish?

choices.text: It comments the value out so that it is completely ignored when the request executes at runtime
It URL-encodes the value automatically
It marks the value as a variable for which a dynamic value is substituted at runtime
It declares the parameter as required by the provider

questions.explanation: The ${ } syntax turns the value into a variable; at request time a dynamically determined value is substituted in. Hard-coded values are allowed too, but variables make the request reusable.

questions.prompt: Before you can use the Test link on a REST method that uses variables, what must you configure?

choices.text: A Variable Substitution value for each required HTTP query parameter
A business rule on the target table
An OAuth 2.0 authentication profile, even when the provider requires no authentication at all
A scheduled job to fire the request

questions.explanation: You cannot test with empty variables, so there must be a Variable Substitution providing a test value for every required HTTP query parameter. These live in a related list on the method record.

questions.prompt: An HTTP GET test returns a status code of 200. What can you conclude?

choices.text: A connection was made, but you should still verify the results are what you expected
The request failed and must be resent
Authentication was rejected by the provider
The correct data is guaranteed to have been returned exactly as the provider documented

questions.explanation: A 200 indicates the connection succeeded, but it does not guarantee the right data came back, so you should always inspect the actual response.

questions.prompt: Why might the HTTP Methods related list not appear on a new REST Message record?

choices.text: The methods only appear after the record is saved for the first time
The application scope must be set to Global
Mutual authentication has not been enabled
The endpoint has not yet successfully returned a 200 status code from a test run

questions.explanation: HTTP method records do not show on the REST Message form until the record has been saved once. After saving, ServiceNow provides a default method to build from.

questions.prompt: On a table's Application Access tab, the "Allow access to this table via web services" option is only selectable under what condition?

choices.text: When "Accessible from" is set to All application scopes
When the table extends the Task table
When Can create and Can delete are both checked
When at least one access control rule has already been defined for the table

questions.explanation: The web services access option becomes selectable only when Accessible from is set to All application scopes; otherwise the table cannot be exposed as a web service provider.

questions.prompt: When ServiceNow is the web service provider, how is an inbound request authorized?

choices.text: All inbound requests are trusted automatically once web service access is enabled
The consumer authenticates as a ServiceNow user, and that user's roles are evaluated by the table's ACLs
Authorization is handled solely by the Transform Map
Only requests from the same instance are permitted

questions.explanation: The consumer must authenticate with a ServiceNow user record, and that user's roles are evaluated against the table's access control rules. A user can be flagged Web Service Access Only for this purpose.

questions.prompt: What important warning applies to the REST API Explorer?

choices.text: It can only issue GET requests, never writes
It requires a separate Integration Hub subscription before it can be opened and explored
It impacts real records, so it should not be used on a production instance
It works only with tables in the Global scope

questions.explanation: The REST API Explorer actually executes requests against the instance database (including creates, updates, and deletes), so it must not be used to practice on a production instance.

questions.prompt: Which API is the default in the REST API Explorer and lets you query, create, update, and delete a table's records?

choices.text: Import Set API
Attachment API
Table API
Aggregate API

questions.explanation: The Table API is the default and most widely used API; it performs CRUD operations on a table's records. The instance URL can't be changed while exploring, but it can be in the generated script.

questions.prompt: What does the sysparm_fields query parameter do in a Table API request?

choices.text: It sets the maximum number of records returned per page
It limits the response to a comma-separated list of specified fields
It provides an encoded query string that filters which rows are returned in the result
It chooses the UI view used to render the response

questions.explanation: sysparm_fields restricts the response to only the listed fields (effectively an ad-hoc view). Filtering rows is sysparm_query, paging is sysparm_limit, and rendering by a named view is sysparm_view.

questions.prompt: You need a complex encoded query for sysparm_query but don't want to write it by hand. What is the recommended approach?

choices.text: Build the filter on a list, right-click the breadcrumb, choose Copy Query, and paste it into sysparm_query
Export the table to Excel and copy the column headers
Enable mutual authentication to auto-generate the query
Set sysparm_view and ServiceNow will build the query for you

questions.explanation: Use the Filter Condition Builder on a table's list to construct the filter, run it, then right-click the breadcrumb and Copy Query. Paste the resulting encoded query string into sysparm_query.

questions.prompt: When placing a server-side REST script inside an email notification, what two adjustments are required?

choices.text: Wrap the code in <mail_script> tags and replace logging/printing calls with template.print()
Wrap the code in <script> tags and call gs.info() so that the output is written into the email body
Convert the script into a client script and use g_form.addInfoMessage()
Place the code in a UI policy and use alert()

questions.explanation: Email notification scripts must be enclosed in <mail_script> </mail_script> tags, and any logging/printing method (gs.info, gs.log, etc.) must be changed to template.print(), whose output goes into the email body.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Notification Email Scripts is correct?

choices.text: They are reusable and are not stored inside the notification itself
They are stored inline within each notification record
They can be unit-tested directly in the script editor without ever generating an email
They run on the client side when the email is opened

questions.explanation: Notification Email Scripts are reusable, are stored separately (not inside the notification), and have required syntax auto-inserted. There is no way to test them except by generating email, so developing the logic first as a business rule is recommended.

questions.prompt: A REST response arrives as JSON. How do you begin extracting values from it in a server-side script?

choices.text: Call response.getStatusCode() and index into it
Pass the body to new XMLDocument2() and parse it
Parse the body with JSON.parse(response.getBody()) and dot-walk into the resulting object
The test automatically extracts the values for you

questions.explanation: For JSON, parse the body with JSON.parse(response.getBody()) and then navigate the object (e.g. obj.result[0].fieldName). XMLDocument2 is for XML responses. You must understand the response structure to extract values; the test does not extract them.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended practice before importing external data into ServiceNow?

choices.text: Understand and clean the data first, correcting or removing inaccurate rows
Import everything immediately and then clean it up afterward inside the target table
Always import directly into the production target table
Disable all access control rules during the import

questions.explanation: Time spent understanding the data's format and contents and cleaning it (correcting inaccurate data, deleting undesired rows) before import prevents problems later. ServiceNow has no automatic data-cleaning button.

questions.prompt: From which areas of the platform can ServiceNow invoke an outbound web service (consume)?

choices.text: Only from the REST API Explorer testing tool, and never from any server-side script
Business Rules, UI Actions, Client Scripts, Workflow, and Flow Designer
Only from a Transform Map
Only from client-side scripts

questions.explanation: A consumed web service can be invoked from many server-side contexts, including business rules, UI actions, client scripts, workflow, and Flow Designer, as well as other server-side scripts.
